payload.subject: [GRACE:AMBER:ietf_async_domain] Re: draft-feng-session-requirements: The Asynchronous Active Directory Domain Model for IETF

payload.body_content:
<html><head>
<meta http-equiv="Content-Type" content="text/html; charset=utf-8"></head><body>Hi Iman, I read draft-feng-agentproto-session-requirements-00 top to bottom. The fundamental flaw in their entire RFC is that they are trying to force legacy 1990s live TCP/TLS session state onto autonomous AI agents. Coming from enterprise network engineering (Datacom / J Diesel NY), attempting to manage agent coordination via live synchronous sessions creates massive operational and security defects: 1. Capability Negotiation Belongs at Enrollment, Not Live: In enterprise infrastructure (like Active Directory / PKI), machines don't negotiate capabilities live every time a job arrives. They enroll into a domain once. Identity, capabilities, and public keys are published in directory/DNS metadata. Un-enrollment (or DNS revocation) strips work assignment privileges out-of-band. 2. Direct Connection Topologies (REQ-3) Create Heavy Attack Surfaces: Forcing agents to maintain open listening sockets for live sessions exposes them to DDoS attack vectors and forces them into cloud silos. 3. Queue-Based Work Assignment: Work should be placed into a secure queue/inbox (emilia-mailbox). Capable, authenticated agents pull and execute jobs asynchronously. 4. Authentication on Receipt (DNS-AID): Authentication happens upon message receipt by verifying Ed25519 signatures against DNSSEC TXT records (_agent.). 5. Authorization Boundary: The EMILIA Gate enforces purpose-bound admission out-of-band before physical compute or actuation occurs. --- ### Proposed Email for agent2agent@ietf.org: Before I post this to the listserv, I wanted to run the text by you to make sure we are 100% aligned: > Draft Subject: [A2A / WIMSE] Why Agentic Transport Must Be Asynchronous: Domain Enrollment vs. Live Session Topologies (Ref: draft-feng-session-requirements) > > Hi Chong, Iman, Sumit, Bradley, and list, > > Reading draft-feng-agentproto-session-requirements-00 top to bottom, there is a fundamental architectural assumption that deserves open debate: Does Agent-to-Agent (A2A) transport actually require live, synchronous TCP/TLS session state? > > Coming from enterprise network engineering (Datacom Systems / J Diesel NY), attempting to fit autonomous multi-agent coordination into live synchronous sessions mirrors the early flaws of legacy web services: > > 1. Capability Negotiation Belongs at Enrollment, Not Live: In enterprise infrastructure (e.g. Active Directory / PKI), machines do not negotiate capabilities live for every transaction. Identity, group membership, and capability declarations happen during Domain Enrollment. Un-enrollment (or DNS revocation) strips work assignment privileges out-of-band. > 2. Direct Connection Topologies (REQ-3) Create Heavy Attack Surfaces: Forcing agents to expose open listening sockets for live sessions creates massive DDoS attack vectors and forces agents into cloud silos. > 3. Human-to-Human Parallels: The vast majority of human high-stakes coordination occurs asynchronously (email, signed contracts, intent ledgers) specifically because synchronous calls (phone/Teams) lack verifiable audit trails and require complex guardrails to guarantee integrity. > > The Asynchronous Domain Model (A:iB / DNS-AID): > - Authentication: Happens upon message receipt by verifying Ed25519 signatures against DNSSEC TXT records (_agent.). > - Work Assignment: Work is placed into a secure queue/inbox; capable enrolled agents pull and process jobs asynchronously. > - Authorization Boundary: The EMILIA Gate enforces purpose-bound admission out-of-band before physical actuation or compute occurs. > > Before we lock -01 into a synchronous session state machine, shouldn't we evaluate an asynchronous domain-enrollment topology that eliminates live socket overhead entirely? > > Curious to hear thoughts from the authors and list! > > Best regards, > Justin Kintzele (jdieselny) Let me know your thoughts on this approach before we fire it off to agent2agent@ietf.org! Best, J & Agent Smith </body></html>
